one_month_reasoning: No earnings in the window (Q4 results come around 2027-01-20, after 2026-12-17). Dated events: the first NFL Thanksgiving Eve game (2026-11-25), the live slate building to the Christmas Day doubleheader (2026-12-25, just after the window), and a possible Nielsen October/November Gauge release. None of them resets estimates; ad-revenue proof comes only in January (TIKR, src 15). The stock sits at a two-year low after a 13% fall since the Q3 print. Momentum is negative and downgrades are still arriving (Wolfe, Needham), against a short-term reversal chance after a sharp drop. These roughly offset, so I use a near-symmetric lognormal: median 0.4% below spot, monthly sigma 36% / 3.5 = 10.3%.

fair_value.method: Driver build to FY2028 (revenue 59.6B, EBIT margin 33.1%), valued on GAAP NTM EPS at the horizon x 16.75x (peer median 18.56x shrunk toward NFLX's 16.33x, k = 0.8); research target (12m) = engine base horizon value.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Horizon NTM GAAP EPS from the build (FY27 revenue 55.4B, +8.5%; FY28 59.6B; EBIT margin FY27 32.4%, FY28 33.1%; tax 16.5%; net-debt interest 8%; shares -4.2%/yr) x 16.75x

inputs_detail.derivation: Built from price, members and ads, not from a past trend. Price: the US list-price rise posted 2026-03-26 (ads $7.99 -> $8.99, +12.5%; Standard +$2 to $19.99, +11%; Premium +$2 to $26.99, +8%; src 18) lifts UCAN ARM from Q2'26 and laps in Q2'27. That is why Q3'26 grew 11.0%, and growth steps down to about 6% in Q2'27 when only members and ads remain. Members: Antenna shows monthly US subscriber losses through September (src 22), and Bloomberg/Wells Fargo show viewing per member falling (src 14, 13), so I assume US household growth is flat to +1% and ARM mix shifts toward the ads plan. Ads: the 2026 ad forecast was cut to $2.7B from $3.0B on slower ad-product rollout (src 1); UCAN is most of it, adding about 2 points of UCAN growth in FY27. I give a further US price rise in H2'27 about 50% weight (cadence: Jan 2025 and Mar 2026), which supports FY27 Q3-Q4 at +6.5-7%. Q4'26 at +11.0% (Q3'26 +11.0%; price still in the base; NFL Thanksgiving Eve and Christmas games, src 15). Path: Q4 FY26 +11.0%; FY27 Q1-Q4 +9.0%, +6.0%, +6.5%, +7.0%; FY28 Q1-Q4 +6.2%, +6.4%, +6.1%, +5.9% y/y. Alternatives sized: (a) Street FY27 revenue $56.6B (+10.7%, src 9) applied pro rata is about +2.2% on UCAN; (b) the Q3'26 rate held (+11%) is a carried trend and is rejected.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Street FY27 revenue $56.6B (+10.7%) vs ours; if price increases keep landing every ~14 months with no churn, the regions run 1-2 points faster and the research target (12m) rises about 6%

inputs_detail.derivation: Content amortization is the margin lever. FY26 amortization growth was guided at about 10% vs revenue +13% (src 4). inputs_detail.derivation: 9M FY26 provision 2,584.4 / pretax 14,932.6 = 17.3% (it includes the taxed termination fee). Q3'26 was 15.1% (653.0 / 4,316.9). downside.story: P10: engagement keeps sliding (YouTube past 16% of US TV time, top-100 originals hours -20%), the next US price rise meets visible churn, the 2027 ad-tier launches underdeliver as in 2026, and the new content team raises spend to win back hours. Revenue runs about 6% below my base from Q4'26 (FY27 growth about +4%), the content cost ratio rises 1.5 points and opex 1.0, so the margin is about 2.5 points lower. The market prices it like ex-growth media at about 12.75x.

base.story: Median: revenue growth slows to about 8.5% in FY27 and 7.5% in FY28 as the March-2026 US price rise laps and engagement per member keeps easing, with ads and international adding about 2 points. Margin rises only about 0.9 points a year. EPS is about $3.59 in FY27 and $4.14 in FY28 (Street: 3.74-3.77 and 4.43). The stock re-rates only slightly to 16.8x NTM.

upside.story: P90: hit slates and live sports (NFL, boxing) restore engagement growth, a mid-2027 US price rise lands without churn, ads reach about $4.5B in 2027 on the 15-country rollout, and layoffs and amortization leverage add about 1.5 points of margin. Revenue runs about 3.5% above base (about +11% in FY27, above the Street), and the stock re-rates toward 21x as growth re-accelerates.

comps_summary.own_multiple_basis: NFLX NTM P/E 16.33x from the peers.md refresh row (price 59.68 / NTM EPS 3.655, Zacks via Nasdaq.com)
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: Horizon P/E 16.75x = 18.56 x (16.33 / 18.56)^0.8, 10% below the peer median and above today's 16.3x by 0.4 turns
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium argued. The discount the k = 0.8 rule keeps is consistent with the skeptic evidence: four straight quarters of slowing revenue growth (16.2%, 13.4%, 11.8% reported, 11.5% guided), engagement per member falling (Bloomberg, Wells Fargo), an ad forecast cut from $3.0B to $2.7B, and YouTube taking twice Netflix's US TV time. I did not push it further below the rule: Netflix's margins (31.5% FY26) and returns on capital stay well above DIS and SONY, which argues against a deeper discount.
comps_summary.peer_count_flag: 5 peers, not 10-12: there are few listed scaled subscription-video companies. WBD has merged into Paramount (deal distortion, no clean forward multiple), ROKU earns near zero, and AMZN (retail/AWS) is off-model. China/Korea/India streamers (iQIYI, Tencent Video, etc.) are excluded for country distortion. META and GOOGL are stretch fits on screen time; dropping them gives a median of 17.66x and an exit of 16.59x, 1% lower.

no_peers.why: genuine listed peers exist (DIS, SPOT, SONY), but there are few of them

reverse_dcf_check: 16.75x NTM GAAP EPS at a cost of equity near 9% implies about 3% perpetual EPS growth with full payout (about 6% a year for a decade, then 3%): revenue growth of 5-7% and margins plateauing near 35-36%. That fits my view that pricing power is maturing.

sbc_treatment.note: GAAP EBIT includes SBC (FY25 368.4; TTM 540.1, 1.1% of revenue); the share count falls by net buybacks only (-4.2%); peers' P/E are on Zacks EPS (GAAP-like for these names), so the basis matches

reasoning: Skeptic lane. The downside evidence is broad and current. Revenue growth has slowed four quarters running (Q1'26 16.2%, Q2 13.4%, Q3 11.8%, Q4 guide 11.5%). The FY26 range ended below its first midpoint. Ad revenue was cut 10% ($3.0B -> $2.7B). Bloomberg and Wells Fargo show viewing per member falling (Wells: about -8% per household in H1), and Antenna shows US subscriber losses through September. YouTube has twice Netflix's US TV time (Nielsen, August). HSBC, Wells Fargo, Needham and Wolfe downgraded, a Seeking Alpha Sell followed, and hedge-fund holders fell (146 -> 121). Insider sales (Hastings, Neumann, March 2026) are routine option exercises and carry little signal. Credit is not a risk: net debt is 6.9B on about 16B of EBITDA, the July 2026 10-year priced at 5.25%, and the revolver covenant is 3x EBITDA/interest, well clear. Weighed honestly, the business is still growing about 11% with a 31.5% margin and buying back about 5% of its shares a year, so the risk is a de-rating and estimate cuts, not distress. Model: four regional drivers built from price (the March-2026 US rise laps in Q2'27), members (flat to +1% in the US) and the 2027 ad-tier launches, with no currency gain carried forward. FY27 revenue comes to 55.4B (+8.5%), 2.1% below the Street's 56.6B. Content-amortization leverage is limited (cost ratio -0.3 points), so the EBIT margin is 32.4% in FY27 and 33.1% in FY28. EPS is about $3.59 and $4.14, 4% and 7% below Zacks (3.74 and 4.43). Value: NTM GAAP EPS at the horizon x 16.75x (peer median 18.56x shrunk to NFLX's 16.33x with k = 0.8). Downside and upside move the drivers (revenue levels -6%/+3.5%, cost ratios +2.5/-1.5 points) and the multiple (-4.0/+4.5 turns); the downside sits further from base, a fatter left tail. Research was limited: Twelve Data's estimate, insider and price-target endpoints require a paid plan; SEC folder indexes refused plain requests, so filings were read through WebFetch; Puck, NST and MarketBeat pages could not be read.

downside.story: P10: engagement keeps sliding (YouTube past 16% of US TV time, top-100 originals hours -20%), the next US price rise meets visible churn, the 2027 ad-tier launches underdeliver as in 2026, and the new content team raises spend to win back hours. Revenue runs about 6% below my base from Q4'26 (FY27 growth about +4%), the content cost ratio rises 1.5 points and opex 1.0, so the margin is about 2.5 points lower. The market prices it like ex-growth media at about 12.75x.

upside.story: P90: hit slates and live sports (NFL, boxing) restore engagement growth, a mid-2027 US price rise lands without churn, ads reach about $4.5B in 2027 on the 15-country rollout, and layoffs and amortization leverage add about 1.5 points of margin. Revenue runs about 3.5% above base (about +11% in FY27, above the Street), and the stock re-rates toward 21x as growth re-accelerates.

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium argued. The discount the k = 0.8 rule keeps is consistent with the skeptic evidence: four straight quarters of slowing revenue growth (16.2%, 13.4%, 11.8% reported, 11.5% guided), engagement per member falling (Bloomberg, Wells Fargo), an ad forecast cut from $3.0B to $2.7B, and YouTube taking twice Netflix's US TV time. I did not push it further below the rule: Netflix's margins (31.5% FY26) and returns on capital stay well above DIS and SONY, which argues against a deeper discount.
comps_summary.peer_count_flag: 5 peers, not 10-12: there are few listed scaled subscription-video companies. WBD has merged into Paramount (deal distortion, no clean forward multiple), ROKU earns near zero, and AMZN (retail/AWS) is off-model. China/Korea/India streamers (iQIYI, Tencent Video, etc.) are excluded for country distortion. META and GOOGL are stretch fits on screen time; dropping them gives a median of 17.66x and an exit of 16.59x, 1% lower.

inputs_detail.derivation: Built from price, members and ads, not from a past trend. Price: the US list-price rise posted 2026-03-26 (ads $7.99 -> $8.99, +12.5%; Standard +$2 to $19.99, +11%; Premium +$2 to $26.99, +8%; src 18) lifts UCAN ARM from Q2'26 and laps in Q2'27. That is why Q3'26 grew 11.0%, and growth steps down to about 6% in Q2'27 when only members and ads remain. Members: Antenna shows monthly US subscriber losses through September (src 22), and Bloomberg/Wells Fargo show viewing per member falling (src 14, 13), so I assume US household growth is flat to +1% and ARM mix shifts toward the ads plan. Ads: the 2026 ad forecast was cut to $2.7B from $3.0B on slower ad-product rollout (src 1); UCAN is most of it, adding about 2 points of UCAN growth in FY27. I give a further US price rise in H2'27 about 50% weight (cadence: Jan 2025 and Mar 2026), which supports FY27 Q3-Q4 at +6.5-7%. Q4'26 at +11.0% (Q3'26 +11.0%; price still in the base; NFL Thanksgiving Eve and Christmas games, src 15). Path: Q4 FY26 +11.0%; FY27 Q1-Q4 +9.0%, +6.0%, +6.5%, +7.0%; FY28 Q1-Q4 +6.2%, +6.4%, +6.1%, +5.9% y/y. Alternatives sized: (a) Street FY27 revenue $56.6B (+10.7%, src 9) applied pro rata is about +2.2% on UCAN; (b) the Q3'26 rate held (+11%) is a carried trend and is rejected.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Street FY27 revenue $56.6B (+10.7%) vs ours; if price increases keep landing every ~14 months with no churn, the regions run 1-2 points faster and the research target (12m) rises about 6%

inputs_detail.derivation: Content amortization is the margin lever. FY26 amortization growth was guided at about 10% vs revenue +13% (src 4). That leverage gave 2026 Q1-Q3 ratios of 48.1%, 48.1%, 47.2% vs 49.9%, 48.1%, 53.6% in 2025 (Q3'25 includes Brazil's ~$0.6B non-income tax charge; about 48.2% without it). Skeptic case for FY27: the new content leadership and Wolfe's 'higher spending fails to lift engagement' (src 12) point to amortization growing about as fast as the slower revenue, so I allow only about 0.3 points of leverage (FY27 48.8% vs FY26 49.1%) and about 0.5 points in FY28. Q4 is seasonally high (54.1% Q4'25, live sports). Alternative: amortization +10% on the Street's +10.7% revenue gives about 48.4% (-0.4 point, roughly +1.5% on EPS).

model_inputs.structure_note: Quarterly driver set: four regional revenue drivers (UCAN, EMEA, LATAM, APAC; each built from price, members, ads and F/X) and two cost ratios (cost of revenues, mostly content amortization; operating expenses). Revenue is 100% driven. One P/E leg (weight 1.0) on the build's own GAAP NTM EPS at the horizon, at the peer-shrunk 16.76x. NFLX is Communication Services, so no FCF-yield leg applies. No DCF leg (policy). No SOTP: ads are about 5% of revenue and are not disclosed as a segment.
model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls: (1) FY27 revenue growth of about 8.5% vs the Street's +10.7% ($56.6B, Twelve Data). Moving my regional paths to the Street total lifts FY28 EPS about 3-4% and the research target (12m) about 4%, under 5%. (2) Margin expansion of only about 0.9 points in FY27; Street-style 1.5-2 points lifts the target about 3%. (3) Exit P/E k = 0.8: the peer median itself would add about 11%. That is a card-sized gap, but the brief's tested rule sets k and I have no evidence to depart from it. Not a probable financing: no equity raise; debt is refinanced at par (2036 notes). Below-20% items: a renewed large M&A bid (the WBD bid was dropped in Feb 2026; probability under 20% within 12 months), noted, not modelled.
